question: The Triadic model helps to explain attitudes and how they are formed. Describe how attitudes can be changed through cognitive dissonance.
markScheme:
- Create a feeling of psychological discomfort / unease / conflict through challenging beliefs (cognitive) / emotions (affective) / behaviour with new information
- Changing one of the components so attitudes are aligned / discomfort is resolved
Accept other appropriate descriptions with reference to specific components of the Triadic model.
Max 3 marks.

question: There are three components which make up our attitude formation according to the triadic model. Describe the three named components of the triadic model.
markScheme:
- Cognitive - what you believe to be true
- Affective - your feelings or emotional response
- Behavioural - your intended behaviour dependent on your attitude
Accept any other relevant descriptions.
Max 3 marks.

question: A rugby union player displays a negative attitude towards defensive drills, which disrupts the performance of the team. When using persuasive communication, explain the factors that need to be considered to change the negative attitude of this player.
markScheme:
- Ensure the messenger is of high status/a significant other/credible, so the player values their opinion
- New information is given so that old beliefs are outweighed, allowing a change in attitude
- The current strength of the attitude will impact success, as a strongly held belief will be more resistant to change
Accept other valid explanations of the factors that need to be considered. Answers must relate to persuasive communication.
Max 3 marks.

question: Elite karate athletes need high levels of fitness to display a positive attitude to training and competition. Explain the term attitude and, using named psychological theories, outline how the negative attitude of a performer towards strength and conditioning training could be changed. Use examples to support your answer.
markScheme:
AO1 - knowledge: an attitude is a belief, value or feeling linked towards an attitude object, made up of the Triadic Model - cognitive, affective and behavioural components. Relevant theories include cognitive dissonance and persuasive communication.
AO2 - application: the cognitive component refers to knowledge/beliefs about strength training, eg 'lifting weights will make me too bulky/is a waste of time'. Persuasive communication may be outlined, eg the messenger should be of high status and deliver a credible, high-quality message containing new information.
AO3 - analysis: linking factors to show impact - eg using cognitive dissonance, by providing new information about the performance benefits of strength training (changing the cognitive component), the athlete may change their behaviour and begin attending sessions regularly. This form of linking/application can be repeated for other theories or components.
Credit other relevant explanation points. Answers must outline, using examples, how the negative attitude could be changed.
Max 8 marks.

question: The performance of a rugby league team can be influenced by the attitudes of its players. Explain how the negative attitude of players can impact on the cohesion of the team.
markScheme:
A - (Definition of attitude) unique feelings and thoughts/Triadic Model/cognitive, affective, behavioural/attitude object
B - Cognitive component - thoughts and opinions
C - Example of negative impact, eg feels training is not worthwhile or equivalent
D - Affective component - emotional feelings
E - Example of negative impact, eg not enjoying training, feels under-valued/discriminated against or equivalent
F - Behavioural component - actions and behaviour
G - Example of negative impact, eg does not participate fully in training, fails to follow agreed tactics or equivalent
H - Decrease in actual productivity of the team/players become part of a faulty process/actual productivity = potential productivity - losses due to faulty processes
I - Poor co-ordination/poor motivation
J - Social loafing - performer 'hides' within the team/reduces effort
K - Ringelmann effect - performance/cohesion may decrease as group size increases
L - (Poor task cohesion) fails to work within the group to achieve a common goal/fails to follow tactics or equivalent
M - (Poor social cohesion) poor social interaction within the group, causes cliques or equivalent
(C, E and G must be linked to a named component of attitude to be awarded a mark; J and K must be explained; L and M need to be in the context of a negative impact on cohesion)
Max 8 marks.

question: The performance of a netball team can be influenced by the attitudes of its players. Explain how the negative attitude of players can impact on the cohesion of the team and, using named psychological theories, describe how a negative attitude may be changed.
markScheme:
A - Cognitive dissonance
B - Attempts to create conflict in thoughts/beliefs/alter one part of the Triadic Model/psychological discomfort
C - Cognitive - give new information/ideas
D - Affective - create new emotions/enjoyment/challenge/motivation or equivalent
E - Behavioural - give success/reinforcement
F - Applied example of any component or all three combined, eg set new goals or give a position of responsibility or equivalent
G - Persuasive communication
H - Status of the messenger/person delivering the information/significant other
I - Quality of the message/new information
J - Situation/time when the message is delivered
K - Individual's resistance to change/strength of current attitude
L - Applied example, eg the coach talks to the player individually and explains the need to change the tactics normally used to help team mates succeed or equivalent
(A and G must be identified to be awarded marks)
Max 8 marks.

question: Many sporting organisations attempt to identify potential elite athletes and help them develop a positive attitude to training and competition. Explain the term attitude and suggest how attitudes are formed.
markScheme:
Attitudes are beliefs/values/feelings/behaviour linked to an attitude object (or equivalent) - sub max of one mark
Triadic Model/cognitive, affective, behavioural components - sub max of one mark
(Past experiences) eg success creates positive emotions/negative experience creates a negative attitude/fear of failure or equivalent - sub max of two marks
(Social learning/socialisation) watching and copying others/peer groups/role models/family/teachers/coaches/media/cultural beliefs/traditions or equivalent/cognitive dissonance/persuasive communication - sub max of two marks
(Conditioning) behaviour followed by rewards encourages repeat behaviour/praise/rewards or equivalent - sub max of two marks
(Familiarity/frequent exposure) increased exposure more likely to form a positive attitude, eg attendance at a club or equivalent - sub max of two marks
Max 3 marks.

question: The captain of a team should be respected and should ensure that all players have a positive attitude. Using one named psychological theory, outline how the negative attitude of an individual or of a team can be changed.
markScheme:
(accept first theory only - theory must be named to be credited)
Persuasive communication:
- Status of messenger/person delivering information/significant other
- Quality of message/new information
- Situation/time when message is given
- Individual's resistance to change
Cognitive dissonance:
- Attempts to create conflict in thoughts/beliefs/alter one part of the Triadic Model/psychological discomfort
- Cognitive - give new information/education
- Affective - create new emotions/enjoyment/fun/feeling of safety or equivalent
- Behavioural - give success/reinforcement
Max 4 marks.

question: Elite squash players have to devote large amounts of time to develop their skills, requiring a positive attitude and high levels of motivation. Name and explain the components of attitudes, giving an example of how a squash player would display a positive 'attitude'.
markScheme:
- Cognitive (component) - believe/think they are training and playing in the correct manner or equivalent
- Affective (component) - positive feelings/emotions/enjoyment or equivalent (not just 'emotional')
- Behavioural (component) - actions of the player/train regularly/compete fairly or equivalent
(Sub max 2 marks)
Use of an applied positive example (cannot be awarded without gaining at least one of the first three points).
Max 3 marks.
